title: Musical director, with McKendrick as business manager
summary: Randolph rehearsed the band and directed the shows while Mike McKendrick handled uniforms, travel and business; endings behind Armstrong were felt rather than written.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, did you rehearse the band or did Louie rehearse it?
What was Mike McKendrick's position in the band?

Mike McKendrick was -- he was more of a what you would call an assistant like -- assistant manger like -- business, boss, business like, tended to the business, you know. Louie didn't care too much for business. He didn't care too much for that. And whatever Mike would do -- he would -- like tell the men where they're going and what they're doing and where to get off, what to wear and things like that, and let's get the uniforms and let's go down around and select uniforms and things like that. He took care of all of that, Mike did.
And you were the musical director?
I was musical director. I took charge of the band and the rehearsing of the band and things like that.
And played any shows -- I had to direct all the shows down there. Louie would come on after the show and they'd do his part. Louie never would get out and direct a show.
I see. On some of the records there's regarded endings. Did you direct those? You know, while Louie is playing a Cadenza --
Yeah, Louie's playing a Cadenza and there's a retard -- did you take care of things like that too or did the guys just feel it after rehearsing?

I think we just felt some of those things. We did. Because -- yeah, we rehearsed those and we felt them. Of course, you'd almost know -- you stay with him awhile and you'd almost know just what he's thinking about or how you're going to breathe.
